header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samantha Lopez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (GreenLake VP Product), Carlos Ruiz (GreenLake Head of ML), Anya Singh (GreenLake CTO), Evan Moore (Infra)
Shared artifacts: https://redwood.ai/decks/model-catalog.pdf, https://redwood.ai/docs/compatibility-matrix.csv
summary: Redwood demo of Model Catalog (API + Console + Optimize). Focus: selecting open models for GreenLake Health workloads, benchmark expectations, compatibility matrix for quantized variants and private deployments, and initial pilot steps. Customer has latency/cost sensitivity and strict data residency/PII constraints; exploring Dedicated vs Private (VPC).
topics: Next steps: benchmark + pricing + security docs
transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Lopez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sam, AE on the Redwood team, with Daniel and Priya from SE. We'll walk through the model catalog, pick open models that map to your latency/cost targets and show the console + API flow.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Thanks, Sam. Our timeline is fairly aggressive — want to get a pilot running in the next 3-4 weeks. Main blockers are PII handling and predictable latency under 300ms p95 for typical queries.
[00:35] Daniel Cho: Great — we'll try to keep that front and center. Quick q: what are your typical sequence lengths and concurrent users?
[00:45] Carlos Ruiz: Most prompts are short, 50-150 tokens, but we have a smaller set of long-form summarization (2k tokens) for care notes. Concurrently it could be 30-100 RPS in peak.
[01:05] Priya Nair: OK that distribution matters a lot for kernel selection and KV cache sizing. In the model catalog we tag models by architecture, tokenization, memory footprint and per-token throughput so you can filter by sequence length profile.
[01:28] Anya Singh: Are those tags accurate for open models? There's a lot of variance between forks and quantized builds.
[01:35] Daniel Cho: Good point. For each model entry we list verified benchmarks on reference hardware and also a compatibility matrix for quantized variants — e.g., 4-bit q8_0 vs 8-bit — and whether the model has been validated on our GPU pool vs CPU. It's in the CSV we shared. Sometimes the transcription shows 'q 8 zero' but the sheet is explicit.
[01:58] Maya Patel: Walk us through picking a model for short prompts where cost is a factor.
[02:10] Samantha Lopez: On the console you can filter by token latency and cost per million tokens, and we show an estimated cost curve. For short prompts we often recommend smaller open models or quantized variants with Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching — that usually hits cost and latency goals.
[02:33] Evan Moore: If we go Dedicated, do we still get those Optimize recommendations? We want autoscaling but also predictable throughput.
[02:42] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated includes the same Optimize toolkit; you can pin model versions, set autoscale policies and define a burst pool. The runtime still uses the same compilation/kernels so performance profiles match.
[03:05] Carlos Ruiz: How do fallbacks work if a model variant isn't available? Will requests hit OpenAI or other providers?
[03:12] Daniel Cho: You configure routing policies. For GreenLake we'd probably prefer fallbacks to other open-model variants or a slightly larger instance instead of public cloud APIs to avoid egress/data residency issues.
[03:30] Maya Patel: Security — SSO, audit logs, KMS — send us the packet.
[03:36] Samantha Lopez: Absolutely, we'll send SOC2, ISO, SAML guides and KMS integration notes. Priya will add KMS examples for customer-side key material.
[03:50] [Speaker 1]: there's a small note in the doc about RBAC for route-level access, we can map that to your teams.
[04:02] Anya Singh: Can you show the compatibility matrix?
[04:10] Priya Nair: Sure — pulling up the CSV. I'll share my screen. (screen share noises) The matrix columns: model, architecture, quantization variants, validated hardware, p95 latency on NVIDA A100/RTX series, memory footprint, notes on tokenizer mismatch. There's also a column for 'recommended profile' used by Redwood Optimize.
[04:40] Priya Nair: Example: LlamaX-33B (open fork) — validated in fp16 on A100, q4_0 provides 3.2x throughput improvement but you see slight accuracy deltas on long-form. For short prompts q4_0 looks fine.
[05:02] Carlos Ruiz: Accuracy deltas — how measured? We need to make sure care-note summarization stays clinically safe.
[05:10] Daniel Cho: We recommend running your eval sets — Redwood has eval harness integration. We can run A/B on their sample prompts and generate metrics for rouge/semantic similarity and hallucination rates. That's part of the benchmark run.
[05:28] Maya Patel: You mentioned tokenizer mismatch — can that break outputs?
[05:33] Priya Nair: Occasionally yes, for forks that change tokenizers. In the catalog we flag tokenizer deviations and provide migration notes. For production we recommend validating on your exact tokenizer and running a KV-cache warm-up.
[05:50] Samantha Lopez: Quick demo: API flow for selecting a model. (typing) In the UI: Models -> Filter by 'short prompt' -> sorted by p95 latency. Select 'LlamaX-7B q4_0' — you can view live benchmarks, sample latency under 50 tokens, and cost estimate. Then click 'Deploy' to stage a variant into a testing pool.
[06:20] [00:06:20] Maya Patel: Is streaming supported for these open models? We have some UI features that expect chunked responses.
[06:27] Daniel Cho: Yes streaming is supported for both hosted and Dedicated. For Private on-prem setups we expose the same streaming API; you just need network rules for persistent connections.
[06:45] Evan Moore: On Private, what about audit logs and retention? We need 7+ years for some records.
[06:53] Priya Nair: Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via TLS with configurable retention. For Private deployments you control the retention window. Hosted customers have configurable retention tiers as an add-on.
[07:10] Carlos Ruiz: Benchmarks — can we run them with our sample workload and also do end-to-end p95 including pre/post-processing?
[07:18] Daniel Cho: Yes. We have a benchmark harness that runs your client-side transforms too; we'll deploy a small runner in your VPC or through a secure tunnel to capture realistic latency. That's part of the run we recommended.
[07:35] Maya Patel: On cost modeling — does Redwood show amortized GPU cost per token?
[07:42] Samantha Lopez: We show cost per million tokens with breakdown by compute, memory, and caching savings. Optimize provides suggestions like enabling prefix cache for repeated prompts and batching windows to reduce per-token cost.
[07:58] Anya Singh: For the long-form 2k token summarizations, do you recommend a different model profile?
[08:05] Priya Nair: For long sequences we recommend models validated for long-context or models with specialized attention kernels. In the catalog you can filter by "long-context" and see validated throughput and KV-cache hit rates. Often teams use a smaller, dedicated pool for short prompts and a separate large-model pool for long-form tasks.
[08:28] [00:08:28] Maya Patel: If we pick two pools, can Redwood route by API key or route rules?
[08:34] Daniel Cho: Routing policies can be per-route, per-key, or payload-based. You can define rules in the console or via API. Example: route anything with header X-Task:long to the long-form pool.
[08:50] Carlos Ruiz: Does the compatibility matrix include compiler/kernel notes? We care about AOT vs JIT kernels for latency.
[08:57] Priya Nair: Yes — matrix includes kernel recommendations and whether we used Triton, TorchInductor, or our internal kernels. There's also a note on sequence-length breakpoints where certain kernels swap.
[09:12] Samantha Lopez: Quick pause — any blockers so far?
[09:16] Maya Patel: PII handling and the SOC2 packet.
[09:20] Samantha Lopez: We'll attach the security packet to the CRM and Priya will include KMS examples.
[09:26] [00:09:26] Anya Singh: About quantization — if we quantize to 4-bit and see accuracy loss, can Redwood roll back automatically?
[09:35] Daniel Cho: You control rollout policies. We support canary and A/B with automatic rollback if quality metrics drop beneath thresholds you define. Redwood's Optimize can monitor eval metrics and trigger rollbacks.
[09:52] Carlos Ruiz: For the benchmark, what hardware will you run on? Our internal expectation is A100.
[09:57] Daniel Cho: We can run on A100 and also on our cost-optimized RTX pool to show delta. The compatibility matrix flags which hardware was used for each measured point.
[10:12] Maya Patel: Any limitations for model size on Dedicated?
[10:16] Priya Nair: You can reserve GPUs with appropriate memory. For very large models we offer sharded inference with KV cache offloading and the catalog notes memory footprint and recommended shard counts.
[10:30] Samantha Lopez: Demo: console Optimize tab — here's recommended batching settings for LlamaX-7B q4_0 given your 50-150 token distribution. It suggests batch size 8, parallelism 2, and prefix cache enabled for repeated prompts, which reduces cost by about 22% in the simulated run.
[10:55] Evan Moore: Can we see logs for token-level attribution and costs?
[11:00] Priya Nair: Yes, per-token tracing can be enabled for debug windows and we show token-level cost breakdown in the console; you can disable it for production to save overhead.
[11:18] [00:11:18] Maya Patel: What's the pilot scope you'd recommend? 2 models, one for short prompts and one for long-form?
[11:25] Daniel Cho: That's our recommended approach: pick a low-cost short-prompt model (e.g., LlamaX-7B q4_0) and a long-context model (e.g., LongLlama-13B fp16) and run parallel A/B tests for a 2-week pilot. We'll run benchmarks and provide quality/regression reports.
[11:44] Carlos Ruiz: Will we get the raw transcripts from the benchmark harness for analysis?
[11:48] Samantha Lopez: Yes, we'll provide the raw outputs, eval metrics and a summary deck.
[11:55] Priya Nair: Also, small note: tokenizer differences sometimes cause length mismatches. In the matrix we include tokenization mapping and a small script to normalize tokenization.
[12:12] Anya Singh: About private deployment: what parts remain in Redwood control plane vs customer control plane?
[12:19] Priya Nair: In Private we provide a control plane for orchestration but you host the serving plane; networking, KMS, logs are customer-controlled, and we can offer an air-gapped installer for on-prem.
[12:38] Maya Patel: Cost question again — how do caching savings show up on billing?
[12:43] Samantha Lopez: Caching reduces billed tokens for repeated prefixes, and the billing UI shows net tokens saved. For Dedicated we can show projected monthly savings based on measured cache hit rates.
[12:58] [00:12:58] Carlos Ruiz: Any caveats when moving from hosted to Dedicated re: model versions?
[13:04] Daniel Cho: Model versions stay consistent; you can pin versions. The main caveat is hardware differences; we recommend re-running short perf tests when changing underlying GPUs.
[13:20] Maya Patel: Can we get a compatibility matrix row for each model that includes: tokenizer, quantization options, validated hardware, per-token latency at 50/150/2k tokens, memory footprint, recommended shard counts?
[13:32] Priya Nair: Yes — that's exactly how the CSV is structured. We'll add a column for 'clinical safe-to-use' notes after your eval.
[13:46] Samantha Lopez: Next steps recap: We'll send the pricing and Dedicated proposal, share the compatibility CSV and benchmark worksheet, set up the benchmark runner, and follow up with the security packet.
[13:59] Maya Patel: Sounds good. Can we schedule the technical deep-dive for Monday?
[14:03] Samantha Lopez: We'll aim for Monday 10am PT. I'll send invites.
[14:10] Evan Moore: Small infra question — do you support private peering to our VPC?
[14:14] Priya Nair: Yes, private peering and AWS PrivateLink are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments.
[14:25] Carlos Ruiz: One last Q — do you have an internal benchmark for hallucination rates?
[14:31] Daniel Cho: We measure hallucination proxies like factuality score against labeled sets and include that in the eval harness; we'll run it on your prompts too.
[14:44] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll wait for the materials.
[14:47] Samantha Lopez: Thanks all — we'll follow up.
[14:52] [00:14:52] (meeting ends)
